descriptors.definition: Professional ethics comprises personal, organizational, and corporate standards of behavior expected from professionals to uphold public interest and trust. Chartered Accountants must abide by ethical codes and fundamental principles to ensure professional credibility and independence.
inclusion: Ethical standards of behavior for Chartered Accountants
Public interest responsibilities
Disciplinary mechanisms for deviations
exclusion: Detailed structures of Part 1, 2, and 3 of the Code
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general moral principles by its specific application to professional chartered accountancy duties and statutory responsibilities.

descriptors.concept_name: Overview of the Code of Ethics
descriptors.definition: The revised Code of Ethics is structured into distinct parts covering all professional accountants, those in service, and those in public practice. It incorporates specific independence standards for audit, review, and other assurance engagements alongside a comprehensive glossary.
inclusion: Professional accountants in service
Professional accountants in public practice
Independence for audit, review, and assurance engagements
exclusion: Detailed behavioural rules outside the structural layout
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between general fundamental compliance requirements and specific engagement-based independence standards.

descriptors.definition: Professional accountants must observe fundamental principles including integrity, objectivity, professional competence and due care, confidentiality, and professional behaviour. Integrity requires straightforwardness and honesty, while professional competence and due care mandate maintaining requisite technical knowledge and acting diligently.
inclusion: Compliance requirements for honesty and fair dealing
Diligence in accordance with technical and professional standards
Avoidance of bias, conflict of interest, or undue influence
exclusion: Detailed safeguards and threat evaluation mechanics
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes core personal and professional ethical traits from specific operational threat categories.

descriptors.concept_name: Threats, Evaluation of Threats and Safeguards
descriptors.definition: The conceptual framework requires professional accountants to identify, evaluate, and address threats to compliance with fundamental principles. These threats are categorized into self-interest, self-review, advocacy, familiarity, and intimidation threats.
inclusion: Identification and evaluation of threats
Categories of threats impacting professional judgment
Examples of circumstances creating self-interest threats
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes active risks to professional independence from the static foundational ethical principles.

descriptors.definition: Non-compliance with laws and regulations comprises intentional or unintentional acts of omission or commission contrary to prevailing laws by clients, employers, management, or those charged with governance. Professional accountants encountering potential NOCLAR during professional services must apply professional judgment without needing exhaustive legal expertise or conducting full investigations.
inclusion: Acts contrary to prevailing laws by clients or employing organizations
Awareness of non-compliance during service provision
Application of professional judgment within engagement scope
exclusion: Personal misconduct unrelated to business activities
Non-compliance by outside parties not listed in the definition
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general audit procedures by focusing specifically on legal and regulatory breaches encountered rather than financial statement assertions.

descriptors.definition: Membership details are entered into the Register upon application acceptance, recording particulars such as qualifications and certificate status. Section 8 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 enumerates explicit statutory disabilities that debar persons from entering or bearing their name on the Register.
instrument_references: Section 8 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
Section 19 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
inclusion: Particulars included in the Register
Statutory disqualifications for membership
Consequences of failing to disclose membership disabilities
exclusion: Classification categories of Associates and Fellows
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes administrative membership registration particulars from absolute statutory grounds for disqualification.

descriptors.concept_name: Disabilities for the Purpose of Membership
descriptors.definition: Section 8 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 outlines specific legal conditions that prevent individuals from being registered or retaining membership. Disqualifications include minority age, unsound mind, insolvency, conviction for moral turpitude, or prior removal for professional misconduct.
instrument_references: Section 8 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
Section 5 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
inclusion: Age and mental capacity criteria
Insolvency and criminal conviction conditions
Removal from membership consequences
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes permanent or conditional legal disqualifications from standard fee-based removal provisions.

descriptors.concept_name: Types of Members of the Institute
descriptors.definition: Members of the Institute are classified into Associates and Fellows pursuant to Section 5 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949. Associate members use the designation A.C.A., whereas members meeting continuous practice criteria or possessing equivalent experience qualify as Fellows using F.C.A.
instrument_references: Section 5 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
inclusion: Criteria for Associate status
Criteria for Fellow status based on continuous practice or equivalent experience
Provisions for name removal from the Register
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes entry-level Associate membership from advanced Fellow membership based on experience and practice duration.

descriptors.concept_name: Removal of Name from the Register
descriptors.definition: Section 20 empowers the Council to remove a member's name from the Register for reasons such as death, request, non-payment of fees, or statutory disabilities. Subsequent restoration mechanisms and penalties for falsely claiming membership are enforced under separate statutory sections.
instrument_references: Section 24 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
Regulation 19 of the Chartered Accountants Regulations, 1988
inclusion: Grounds for council removal of members
Fee default removal conditions
Introduction to membership restoration and penalties
exclusion: Detailed case studies of fraudulent claims
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes administrative or penal removal from the Register from initial registration criteria.

descriptors.definition: Regulation 19 and Section 20 govern the restoration of a member's name to the Register following removal for non-payment of fees or disciplinary orders. Falsely claiming membership or practice status without valid credentials attracts penal consequences under Section 24.
instrument_references: Section 20 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
Section 24 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
inclusion: Restoration application processes and effective dates
Penalties for falsely representing membership
Judicial precedents on unauthorized designations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes regular membership maintenance from the reinstatement process of canceled registrations.

descriptors.concept_name: Penalty for Falsely Claiming to be a Member etc.
descriptors.definition: Section 24 penalizes any non-member who represents themselves as an Institute member or uses the Chartered Accountant designation, as well as members lacking a certificate of practice who claim to be in practice. Convictions entail fines and potential imprisonment.
instrument_references: Section 24 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
Section 6 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
inclusion: Fines and imprisonment terms for first and subsequent convictions
Significance of holding a Certificate of Practice
Prohibition on unauthorized professional practice
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes infractions involving false professional titles from standard internal disciplinary code violations.

descriptors.definition: A practicing Chartered Accountant is a member holding a valid Certificate of Practice or deemed to be in practice under the Act. Members not in practice are restricted from accepting professional engagements typically reserved for Chartered Accountants.
instrument_references: Section 6 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
Chartered Accountants Act and its Regulations
inclusion: Certificate of practice mandatory requirement
Annual fee obligations for practice certificates
Restrictions on members not holding a certificate of practice
exclusion: General membership registration without practice rights
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes passive institute members from active practitioners entitled to render statutory professional services.
